title: Srikanth Falls in the Final. India's Best US Open in Years Still Ends One Match Short.
excerpt: The former world number one fought back from a game down but was overwhelmed 9-21 in the decider by Chinese Taipei's Su Li-Yang in Fullerton. Three Indians had reached the semifinals — the deepest run by an Indian contingent at the tournament.
body:
Kidambi Srikanth's dream run at the US Open Super 300 ended in heartbreak on Sunday as he fell 15-21, 21-16, 9-21 to Chinese Taipei's Su Li-Yang in the men's singles final in Fullerton, California. The 33-year-old former world number one fought his way back into the match after losing the opening game but was overwhelmed in a lopsided decider.

It was a bittersweet ending to what had been Srikanth's most commanding tournament performance in months. The Indian had beaten Malaysia's Lee Zii Jia in straight games in the round of 16, survived a three-game battle against Chinese Taipei's Jhuo-Fu Liao in the quarterfinals, and saved three match points against Japan's fourth seed Yudai Okimoto to reach his first final of the season.

## A Familiar Pattern

The final followed a pattern that has haunted Srikanth in recent years — bursts of brilliance punctuated by stretches where unforced errors take over.

Su, ranked 46th in the world and nine years Srikanth's junior, raced to a 7-2 lead in the opening game. Srikanth clawed his way back to 10-10, but the 24-year-old's pace and court coverage proved too much after the interval. Su closed out the first game 21-15 in just 17 minutes.


![Lee Zii Jia — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/eb/Lee_%26_Ng_President%27s_Cup_2023_%28cropped%29.jpg)



> **"## India's Biggest US Open Contingent

The final was the culmination of a breakthrough US Open for Indian badminton."**



The second game was more competitive. Srikanth built a 7-4 lead and maintained control through the interval. When Su's smashes started to find their mark and the Taipei youngster surged to 14-10, it looked like the match would slip away entirely. But Srikanth summoned the aggressive strokeplay that once made him a world number one, reeling off a series of powerful smashes to level the match at one game apiece with a 21-16 win.

The decider, though, was no contest. Su was relentless from the start, building a four-point lead by the interval and never letting Srikanth back in. The Indian managed just nine points in the third game as Su's speed and precision exposed the gaps in Srikanth's defence.


## India's Biggest US Open Contingent

The final was the culmination of a breakthrough US Open for Indian badminton. Three Indians — Srikanth, 18-year-old Rounak Chouhan, and Devika Sihag — reached the semifinals, the largest Indian presence at that stage of the tournament in recent memory.

Chouhan's run was the most remarkable of all. Playing in his first-ever Super 300 event, the teenager had stunned world number six Chou Tien Chen in the second round and beaten Israel's Misha Zilberman in the quarterfinals before Su ended his run in the semis with a 21-17, 21-19 win.


![Yudai Okimoto — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/46/Okimoto_Yudai%E6%B2%96%E6%9C%AC%E5%84%AA%E5%A4%A7_%28cropped%29.jpg)


Devika Sihag, meanwhile, won the opening game against Denmark's second seed Line Christophersen but could not sustain the intensity, going down 21-15, 11-21, 15-21.

## The Diaspora Angle

The tournament in Fullerton, a short drive from Los Angeles, drew strong support from the Southern California Indian community. With Indian badminton players increasingly competing on American soil — and the sport's inclusion in the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics on the horizon — events like the US Open carry growing significance for the diaspora.

For Srikanth, who won the 2021 World Championships silver medal and was once ranked as high as number one in the world, the final appearance is a reminder that his competitive fire still burns — even if the legs do not always cooperate over three games.

Chouhan, at 18, represents the next wave. If his US Open performance is any indication, Indian badminton's pipeline is in good health.
